chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amriki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife before consummating the marriage, and she claimed she was pregnant. He said: 'If evidence is established that he lowered his garment (consummated), and then he denies the child, he will curse her, and then they will be separated, or the full dowry is due upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his wife before consummation but she claims to be pregnant?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific application of *li'an* when a husband denies paternity after a pre-consummation divorce, contingent upon proof that he 'lowered the veil' (consummation). It highlights the juristic nuance that if consummation is established, the full dowry (*mahr*) becomes due alongside the separation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on evidentiary standards in marital disputes.
